# DNS tunnel engine — not bundled, and exactly what is missing

This build ships no DNS tunnel engine. `DnsTunnelController` reports
`UNAVAILABLE` and the app never shows a tunnel as connected. This file records
why, and what has to be added.

## Why it is not here

The engine has to be a real implementation of a DNS tunnel protocol. The
canonical one is **dnstt** (David Fifield, `www.bamsoftware.com/software/dnstt/`),
a Go program with a client and a server.

It could not be fetched from the environment this branch was written in:

- `https://www.bamsoftware.com/git/dnstt.git` — the outbound proxy answers
  `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`.
- GitHub mirrors — this session's git credentials are scoped to
  `meysam82003/Ghajarvpn-` only, so any other repository fails
  authentication.

Writing the build script and the invocation from memory was the alternative
and was rejected. A pinned commit hash that is wrong produces a build failure;
worse, **command-line flags that are wrong produce a client that exits and
gets reported as the network blocking the tunnel** — the most expensive kind
of wrong answer this app can give. Reimplementing the protocol in Kotlin was
also rejected: dnstt's transport is a KCP/smux stack over a Noise handshake,
and untested, unreviewed crypto written against no test vectors would be worse
than having no tunnel.

So the client is implemented against a stated contract, and the contract is
below.

## What must be added

### 1. The binary

Built exactly the way `scripts/build-singbox.sh` builds sing-box — a Go
program cross-compiled per ABI with the NDK's clang — and installed as:

```
app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libdnstt.so
app/src/main/jniLibs/armeabi-v7a/libdnstt.so
```

**The name is load-bearing.** Android extracts and marks executable only files
matching `lib*.so`. A Go binary called anything else cannot be run from
`nativeLibraryDir` at all. This is the same constraint that made sing-box a
`libsingbox.so`, and `AetherController` already execs `libaether.so` this way.

### 2. Its licence

Vendor the upstream licence file into this directory, unmodified, and note the
commit it came from. Do not ship the binary without it.

### 3. The invocation

`DnsTunnelController.start` is the only place that needs changing. It must:

- exec `nativeLibraryDir/libdnstt.so` with the profile's resolver, domain and
  server public key;
- have the client listen on `DnsTunnelController.LOCAL_PORT` (18753);
- observe the engine's own "listening" line on stdout/stderr before reporting
  `LISTENING` — **not** report it after a sleep;
- treat a non-zero exit as `FAILED` with the engine's last line as the detail.

### 4. What the server side needs

The operator of the tunnel server must provide, and the user must enter:

| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| Domain | A zone delegated to the tunnel server, e.g. `t.example.com`. The server must be the authoritative nameserver for it. |
| Public key | The server's key, printed by the server on first run. The client verifies the far end with it. |
| Resolver | Any recursive resolver that will carry TXT queries for that zone. The DNS laboratory tests this per resolver. |

None of the three is guessable and none is generated by this app.

## What is already real and testable without the binary

- The per-resolver tunnel-path test in `DnsScanEngine`: a TXT query under a
  random label of the user's own domain, which passes only if an answer
  returns from the zone's own nameserver. Random label every time, because a
  cached answer would only prove the resolver has a cache.
- `DnsResolverStore.bestCandidate(tunnelOnly = true)`, which will only ever
  select a resolver whose tunnel path was tested and worked.
- The profile screen's validation, and `dnsTunnelConfigured`.
- `DnsTunnelPhase`, which distinguishes "engine missing" from "profile
  incomplete" from "failed" — three states that a single boolean would have
  flattened into one unhelpful error.
